purpose: Special-function benchmark stage: accuracy and speed of RapidGLM's special functions (include/rapidglm/vmath.hpp: RapidGLM's log, log1p, exp, digamma and trigamma, the C library's lgamma) against glibc's libm and boost::math (C++), NumPy and SciPy (Python) and base R, single-threaded
status: Development measurements for the merge decision, not the formal 1.5.0 numbers (those come from the 1.5.0 receipts run, which re-measures this stage under the full protocol). C++ accuracy and speed: build F (branch vmath before the rebase, its code equal to the commit except the branch that evaluates out-of-domain vector lanes of log and log1p at 1), speed on efficiency core 16 under the shared lock after the quiet-host check; another session's 8-thread job started on cores 24-31 during the speed stage (minima over repeated in-cache calls agree with earlier quiet runs to 0.1 ns). Python and R: not timed under the lock (the host stayed above the quiet threshold), run on performance core 5 (capped at 2.2 GHz, load about 8) with the final code; rapidglm and the comparator run on the same core, so their ratio is the measurement.
build_F_log1p_note: Build F's AVX2 log1p over log-uniform (1e-300, 1e-5) took 140 ns an element: lanes below 2^-60, which the scalar code then replaces, were first evaluated in the vector path with subnormal intermediates. The committed code evaluates such lanes at 1 first: 5.9 ns on CPU 5 (performance_core_untimed), same bits.
commit_of_build_F: 4e2b39a + uncommitted vmath changes (later commit 2cfae98 after the rebase onto fc2705a)
